description:
FILED s470bl (Opus, 2026-09-05) while shipping #1022 half (b); measured, not
assumed, and the measurement made it much narrower than the design feared.

The #1022(b) licence (Pl::PExpr::TokenUtils::calls_user_code) is SYNTACTIC: it
sees a named call, a method call, a code-ref call, `goto`, `eval`, `require`,
`tie`.  User code reached through MAGIC carries no marker at all, so a loop
whose body is `$a + $b` takes no frame even though an overloaded `+` runs a
sub.

WHAT PERL DOES, probed 5.40.3 -- it refuses these exits itself:

  use overload '+' => sub { last };   for (1..3) { my $z = $v + 1 }
    perl: Can't "last" outside a loop block      PCL: the same
  use overload '""' => sub { last };  for (1..3) { my $z = "$s" }
    perl: Can't "last" outside a loop block      PCL: the same
  sub FETCH { last }  tie my $t,"T"; for (1..3) { my $z = $t }
    perl: Can't "last" outside a loop block      PCL: the same
  sub DESTROY { last }  for (1..3) { { my $d = bless {},"D" } }
    perl: n=303 (the `last` does nothing)        PCL: n=303 (PCL runs no
                                                 scope-exit DESTROY, so it
                                                 agrees by another route)

So PCL's rule "no frame => die with perl's text" AGREES with perl in every
one-loop shape.

THE ONE DIVERGENCE is an OUTER loop that DOES hold a frame: the throw is
caught there.

  sub FETCH { last }
  tie my $t, "T"; my $n = 0;
  for my $o (1..2) { for my $i (1..3) { $n++; my $z = $t; $n += 100 }
                     $n += 10000; f() }  sub f {}
    perl: Can't "last" outside a loop block
    PCL:  n=1     (the inner loop is frame-less; the outer one caught it)

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the exit site would have to know it is inside a magic
callback.  Cheap version: bind *p-dyn-loop-frames* to 0 around every
overload/tie/DESTROY/%SIG dispatch -- one special bind per DISPATCH, which is
a per-operation cost on the overload path, so measure `ovlsub` before doing
it.  Not attempted here.

=== CLOSED (s470bl) BY THE #1162 LICENCE, not by a separate fix ===
The one divergence this task recorded was the nested spelling: an OUTER loop
holding a frame caught a throw perl refuses.  Under the reachability licence
that outer loop takes no frame either â it only calls a sub that cannot exit â
so the tie `FETCH` doing `last` now dies with perl's own
`Can't "last" outside a loop block`, exactly as perl does.  Re-probed
(`scratch/s470bl/p/r04-tie-outer.pl`): perl and PCL agree.
subject: CLOSED by the #1162 narrowing (s470bl): with the reachability licence an overload/tie/DESTROY `last` dies exactly as perl does, in the nested spelling too
